patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wix documents a broader use-case set; Medusa is narrower/specialist.

General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than Wix's shape. Choose Wix only if your buying job matches “Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell onlin” rather than Medusa's shape. Workflow advantage: Medusa leans shared coverage; Wix leans checkout-conversion, catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wix documents a broader use-case set; Medusa is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax.; Wix is Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell online), Business $39, Business Elite $159 (annual tile.
- Company-size focus: Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Wix (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Medusa-leaning — vs Wix-leaning checkout-conversion, catalog-management, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Wix — Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B.

Limitations — Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce); Wix: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B; Plan gates for selling start at Core — Free/Light are not store plans.
